resources.string: Upload files and folders from your phone to GitHub.

Paste a GitHub personal access token that can write to your repositories: a classic token with the “repo” scope, or a fine-grained token with “Contents: Read and write”. The token stays in memory only, is sent only to api.github.com over HTTPS, and is forgotten when you close the app.
Pick the repository and branch that should receive your files. Only repositories your token can write to are listed (up to 500, most recently updated first), and the default branch comes first.

Add single files or whole folders. In a folder everything is ticked by default, so just untick what you don’t want. The folder structure is kept, and you can choose a destination folder inside the repository. Small files are bundled into a few commits; large files are sent one by one at a pace GitHub’s rate limits allow. Files that are already in the repository with identical content are skipped, so an interrupted upload can simply be run again. Not supported: files over 95 MB, and empty folders (Git doesn’t store them).
Destination folder in the repository (optional, e.g. photos/2026/)
Files that were already committed stay in the repository. You can run the upload again later; files that are already up to date are skipped.
